messages:
lexi-support: Heads-up — customer 'AcmePayments' opened a P1 ticket: their p99 latency for text-generation jumped from ~2.1s to ~9s around 09:20 UTC. They attached screenshots of our dashboard and a curl request. Link: https://dash.redwood/acme/requests (private)

maria-sre: copying the key metrics they pasted. Their sample: p50=350ms p95=760ms p99=9.2s error-rate=0.2%

sam-eng: do we know if they hit a different model variant? anything changed in routing/policies last hour?

lexi-support: they've been pinned to model:redwood-13b-v2 but the request shows `model_override: redwood-13b-v2-quant` in their payload logs. No config change on their side.

maria-sre: hm. I checked high-level dashboards — cluster-level pod CPU looks normal, but the per-instance histograms show one host with a long tail. Possible aggregation mismatch.

jen-oncall: flagging an observability pitfall: dashboard A uses `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(rw_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))` while dashboard B was showing `quantile_over_time(0.99, rw_request_latency[5m])` per instance then averaged. Those are not mathematically equivalent.

sam-eng: can you post the exact PromQL you've used? I want to repro locally.

maria-sre: sure — the cluster-wide query I ran: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(rw_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, cluster))
```
And the dashboard we inherited does per-host quantiles then `avg()` across hosts: 
```
avg(quantile_over_time(0.99, rw_request_latency[5m])) by (cluster)
```
This explains part of the delta when a single host has a spike. Aggregating host quantiles can hide long-tail impacts or amplify them depending on distribution.

lexi-support: customer insists it's a regression — they saw a 3x increase with no traffic change. We need a mitigation ASAP.

maria-sre: quick checks:
- which host is the outlier: `topk(5, increase(rw_request_latency_sum[5m]) / increase(rw_request_latency_count[5m])) by (instance)`
- check recent deploys: `kubectl get rs -n inference --show-labels --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp`
- check model variant routing logs (sam, can you grep router logs for their account id?)

sam-eng: on it. Grepping now. I see a canary rollout for `redwood-13b-v2-quant` started at 09:10 and targeted 5% traffic. Routing policy fallback kicks in for model size mismatch and will route to a host running the quantized kernel that has a slightly different execution path.

perf-bot: automated note: increased retry_count for account AcmePayments from 0 -> 2 between 09:15-09:25. (source: ops telemetry)

jen-oncall: retries would amplify tail. If a slow host causes retries, p99 will balloon. Also quantized kernels sometimes add variability if kernel selection picks a fallback path.

maria-sre: I pulled raw buckets for the customer timeframe — attached snippet: 
```
# instance=infra-13b-2
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="0.1"} 1200
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="0.5"} 2400
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="1"} 3000
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="5"} 3050
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="10"} 3055
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="+Inf"} 3060
# instance=infra-13b-9   <-- outlier
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="0.1"} 300
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="0.5"} 600
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="1"} 650
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="5"} 1200
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="10"} 1500
rw_request_latency_bucket{le="+Inf"} 1505
```
You can see instance infra-13b-9 has many more requests in the >5s bucket. That will push cluster histogram p99 up when summed. But per-host quantile avg might look different.

sam-eng: infra-13b-9 logs show intermittent OOM-kernel fallbacks and a couple of CUDA driver warnings around 09:12. I suspect a degraded GPU path for quantized kernels on that host.

lexi-support: customer provided a reproducible curl: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"<1000-char prompt>","account_id":"acme-123"}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate
```
They say 1 in 20 requests hit the slow tail.

maria-sre: mitigation options now: 
1) rollback the canary of `-quant` (fast)
2) update routing to avoid infra-13b-9 for that model variant (targeted, requires router patch)
3) increase host count to dilute the outlier (adds cost)
4) add a short-circuit: if instance latency > 3s then auto-failover to non-quant variant for that request (needs quick patch)

jen-oncall: I vote rollback canary until we root-cause kernel fallback. Also add a dashboard panel to show `sum(rate(rw_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance)` so we can see per-instance bucket rollups.

sam-eng: rolling back canary now — command: `kubectl patch deployment/router -n inference -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"canary-redwood-13b-v2-quant":"false"}}}}}'`

ops-bot: deploy event: router canary rollback started by sam-eng at 09:34 UTC.

perf-bot: metric check in 5m: cluster p99 fell from 8.9s -> 1.1s after rollback (prelim).

lexi-support: relaying to customer: "we rolled back a model canary that correlated with the spike — can you try again and paste the request id if you see a slow request?"

maria-sre: follow-up notes for postmortem: 
- root cause likely quantized kernel fallback on a specific host causing long-tail.
- observability confusion due to two dashboards using different aggregation strategies (aggregate histograms vs avg of per-host quantiles). Add doc explaining why those differ.
- action items: 1) add per-instance bucket panel, 2) instrument router to tag requests that triggered kernel fallback, 3) add an alert when topk(1, increase(rw_request_latency_bucket[5m]) by (instance)) diverges by >x from median cluster host, 4) run canary on smaller traffic with telemetry to detect kernel fallbacks.

jen-oncall: also update runbook: if p99 spike: check per-instance buckets -> check recent canaries -> check retry amplification.

sam-eng: creating a short PR to tweak dashboard and a follow-up to require kernel-fallback logging in canary.

lexi-support: customer confirmed reduced latency after our rollback and will keep ticket open for 24h for verification.

maria-sre: keeping this thread for the postmortem write-up. I'll add the raw queries + Grafana panel links in the PM. Thanks all. :pray:
